name: Ismail Samani
role: Amir of the Samanid Empire from 892 to 907
contribution: The Samanid amir of Transoxiana and Khorasan.
image_credit: Бонки миллии Тоҷикистон (National Bank of Tajikistan) (banknote), Steve Burke (photo) · Public domain

checks.lead: Abū Ibrāhīm Ismā'īl ibn-i Aḥmad-i Sāmāni (Persian: ابو ابراهیم اسماعیل بن احمد سامانی; May 849 – 24 November 907), better known simply as Amir Ismail-i Samani (اسماعیل سامانی), and also known as Isma'il ibn-i Ahmad (اسماعیل بن احمد), was the Samanid amir of Transoxiana (892–907) and Khorasan (900–907). His reign saw the emergence of the Samanids as a powerful force. He was the son of Ahmad ibn-i Asad and a descendant of Saman Khuda, the eponymous ancestor of the Samanid dynasty who renounced Zoroastrianism and embraced Islam.
